company: Donocca SAS (Patio del Vea, San Juan)
stage_or_date: Feb 2026 (concession closed after Carnival holiday; article 2026-02-25)
the_problem: Donocca SAS ran the food court of the Vea supermarket (Cencosud) in San Juan, Argentina, since the pandemic. A 2025 union inspection treated young workers hired under the national PIL programme as off-the-books staff, leading to a lawsuit and a payout of over 150 million pesos. Accounts were embargoed for months, three months of rent plus salaries and suppliers fell behind, and the 2024 and 2025 recessions cut revenue.
the_decision: Concession holder Emanuel Uzair closed the food court for good in February 2026 after paying the lawsuit in instalments and clearing the debt with Cencosud, when Cencosud refused to renew the lease. His reason: 'Llega un punto que estábamos asfixiados económicamente y lo que hacíamos era sobrevivir'; he said the lawsuit cost over 150 million pesos and 'vino la recesión del 2024, la del 2025'.
the_outcome: The food court, open for almost 30 years, closed permanently; 20 families lost their income and could not be relocated. Uzair says no debt remains with Cencosud ('No les quedamos debiendo un peso'). The venue was already being dismantled and a gym franchise is expected to take the space.
